list.subject: Subject
list.emptyHint: Send your first email through the API — POST /emails.

detail.subject: Subject
detail.eventsStalled: No other events will show — SES can only push delivery events to a public https URL, and this deployment doesn't have one. Re-run setup to create the SQS events queue the worker polls instead; new emails then get events within seconds. Emails sent before that stay as they are.

bounceBanner.hard: Hard bounce — this address can't receive mail.
bounceBanner.suppressed: It was added to your suppression list.

insights.emptyHint: It was sent before insights existed, or it hasn't been sent yet. Earlier emails are not analyzed retroactively.
insights.notCheckedWhy: DNS state unavailable at send time.
insights.notApplicableToggle: {count, plural, one {# check not applicable} other {# checks not applicable}}
insights.byDesignNote: MillionSend enforces this structurally — it cannot fail here.

dmarc_record.title: DMARC record
dmarc_record.description: Your sending domain publishes a DMARC policy. Google, Yahoo and Microsoft require one for bulk senders — p=none already satisfies them; p=quarantine or p=reject additionally unlocks BIMI.
dmarc_record.advice: Add a _dmarc TXT record to your domain. Start at p=none, watch the reports, then tighten.

auth_alignment.title: SPF and DKIM alignment
auth_alignment.description: SPF and DKIM pass and align with your From domain — the base requirement of every major mailbox provider.
auth_alignment.advice: Nothing to do — MillionSend verifies SPF and DKIM on your domain before any send leaves.

list_unsubscribe.title: One-click unsubscribe headers
list_unsubscribe.description: The message carries List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers. Gmail and Yahoo require one-click unsubscribe for bulk senders.
list_unsubscribe.advice: Send marketing through broadcasts or topics — MillionSend injects both headers automatically.

link_domains_match.title: Links match your domain
link_domains_match.description: At least one link points at your sending domain. A message whose links all go to third-party domains matches a common phishing shape.
link_domains_match.advice: Link to your own domain at least once, or send from the domain you link to.

no_shorteners.title: No link shorteners
no_shorteners.description: Shortened links (bit.ly, tinyurl and similar) hide the destination and are heavily abused. With click tracking on, a shortener becomes a tracking-wrapped double redirect — a documented phishing pattern for Gmail. youtu.be is YouTube's own share domain and only counts while click tracking would wrap it.
no_shorteners.advice: Use full destination URLs — youtube.com/watch instead of youtu.be. Click tracking already reports what was clicked.

body_size.title: HTML size
body_size.description: Gmail clips messages whose HTML exceeds 102KB — everything past the clip point, unsubscribe footer included, hides behind "View entire message".
body_size.advice: Keep the HTML under 102KB: fewer inlined styles, shorter content, nothing embedded.

plain_text.title: Plain-text version
plain_text.description: The message ships a text/plain part alongside the HTML. HTML-only mail scores worse with spam filters and breaks in text-only clients.
plain_text.advice: Provide a text body with every HTML send.

visible_unsubscribe.title: Visible unsubscribe link
visible_unsubscribe.description: The body contains an unsubscribe link placed before Gmail's clip point. Recipients who can't find it press "Report spam" instead.
visible_unsubscribe.advice: Put an unsubscribe link in the footer and keep it inside the first 102KB of HTML.

phishing_links.title: No phishing-pattern links
phishing_links.description: No link text naming a different domain than its destination, no links to raw IP addresses, no http links claiming to be https — the patterns phishing filters match on.
phishing_links.advice: Make link text agree with the destination and never link to bare IPs.

no_reply_from.title: Replyable From address
no_reply_from.description: The From address is not a no-reply mailbox. Replies are an engagement signal mailbox providers count in your favor.
no_reply_from.advice: Send from a monitored address; if you must use no-reply, set a Reply-To.

svg_images.title: No SVG images
svg_images.description: SVG does not render in most email clients — Gmail and Outlook show a blank where the image should be.
svg_images.advice: Export images as PNG or JPEG.

attachments_marketing.title: No attachments
attachments_marketing.description: Marketing mail with attachments raises spam and malware scores; bulk senders almost never attach files.
attachments_marketing.advice: Host the file and link to it instead.

image_text_ratio.title: Text alongside images
image_text_ratio.description: The message has real visible text next to its images. Image-heavy mail with almost no text is a classic spam signature and unreadable while images are blocked.
image_text_ratio.advice: Write the message as text; use images to support it, not replace it.

tracking_unbranded.title: Branded tracking domain
tracking_unbranded.description: Open and click tracking rewrite links through a tracking host. On a branded subdomain the links stay on your domain; on a shared host your mail borrows someone else's reputation.
tracking_unbranded.advice: Verify a tracking subdomain for your domain so tracked links stay yours.

root_domain_send.title: Marketing on a subdomain
root_domain_send.description: Marketing sent from your root domain ties its reputation to all your mail, transactional included.
root_domain_send.advice: Send marketing from a dedicated subdomain such as news.yourdomain.com.

insecure_links.title: HTTPS links
insecure_links.description: Every link uses https. Plain-http links get flagged by security scanners and can be tampered with in transit.
insecure_links.advice: Serve link targets over https and update the URLs.

subject_lint.title: Subject line
subject_lint.description: The subject avoids all-caps and runs of !!! or ??? — both trip content filters.
subject_lint.advice: Sentence-case the subject and drop the repeated punctuation.

image_alt_text.title: Image alt text
image_alt_text.description: Every image carries alt text — what recipients see while images load or stay blocked, and what screen readers read.
image_alt_text.advice: Give each meaningful image an alt attribute.

images_offsite.title: Images on your domain
images_offsite.description: Images load from your sending domain. Third-party image hosts tie the message's rendering to servers you don't control.
images_offsite.advice: Host images on your own domain.

bimi_ready.title: BIMI readiness
bimi_ready.description: BIMI shows your logo in supporting inboxes. It requires DMARC at p=quarantine or p=reject — p=none is not enough.
bimi_ready.advice: Tighten DMARC to quarantine or reject, then publish a BIMI record with a verified logo.

reply_to_present.title: Reply-To with no-reply From
reply_to_present.description: Sending from a no-reply address with a Reply-To header set, so replies still reach a real mailbox.
reply_to_present.advice: Keep a Reply-To on every send from a no-reply address.

suppressedDrawer.title: Suppressed details
suppressedDrawer.blocked: Sends to this address are blocked to protect your domain reputation. The API returns 422 suppressed_recipient.
suppressedDrawer.step1: Confirm the mailbox exists now — removing early usually re-bounces.
suppressedDrawer.step2: Then remove the suppression; the next send goes through normally.

suppressions.title: Suppressions
suppressions.addBody: Emails to this address will not be sent.
suppressions.removeBody: {email} can receive emails again after removal.
suppressions.emptyHint: Hard bounces and complaints are added automatically.

detail.removeNote: Removing an address that bounced permanently will likely bounce again — remove it only after the mailbox is fixed.

apiSheet.title: Emails API
apiSheet.keyHint: Replace ms_xxxxxxxxx with an API key from the API Keys page. Every SDK also honors the MILLIONSEND_API_KEY and MILLIONSEND_BASE_URL environment variables.
